subject: Spike of 429 rate-limits impacting Novelle Health - investigation & remediation
messages:
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@novellehealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@novellehealth.com, procurement@novellehealth.com
Date: 2026-02-14T14:12:00Z
Subject: sudden 429s since 08:50 ET - lots of failed patient inference calls

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a surge of 429s on our production tenant around 08:50 ET this morning. Our ingestion pipeline for clinical notes has ~300 req/s and roughly 20% of requests (~60 req/s) started failing with 429. Error IDs: req_id=40f3c8a9, 40f3c9b1. This is causing queues to back up and delaying downstream workflows.

Can you confirm whether this is on your side? Any temporary mitigation while you investigate would be helpful; we can throttle on our end but downstream SLAs depend on this throughput.

We have attached a small sample of failing request headers and timestamps.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Kim
Product Ops, Novelle Health
laura.kim@novellehealth.com

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@novellehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-14T14:40:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden 429s since 08:50 ET - lots of failed patient inference calls

Hi Laura — Marissa from Customer Reliability here. Thanks for the sample. We have a live support ticket INC-2026-0458 open and are looking at metrics. Initial findings: your tenant was being evaluated against a per-tenant rate policy that mistakenly used an aggregated shard multiplier during a config rollout; requests were double-counted in the quota check leading to effective throttling.

Immediate mitigation applied (14:38Z): temporarily bypassed the tenant-specific multiplier and set a relaxed quota while we roll back the faulty config. You should see failures drop to near zero in the next 2–3 minutes.

Next steps:
- We'll keep the bypass in place for up to 8 hours while we stabilize and run a targeted smoke test.
- Engineering (cc: Dev) will push a safe rollback of the multiplier rollout and add a validation gate.
- We'll share a concise timeline and a postmortem draft within 72 hours.

Apologies for the impact — we'll also propose a goodwill credit for the window affected.

Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (CSV stub)

Date: 2026-02-14T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden 429s since 08:50 ET - quick root-cause and rollback plan

Folks — quick technical note for the record and for Laura:

Root cause (prelim): a canary rollout of a tenant quota multiplier introduced an unintended code path where autoscale-adjusted shard counts were multiplied twice during the rate-limit check. For burst patterns (like Novelle's) this resulted in effective quota reductions and 429s.

Action taken: rollback of the multiplier rollout started at 14:42Z and completed at 14:49Z; we also applied a temporary bypass to the quota check for your tenant.

Planned follow-ups:
- Add unit + integration tests to validate multiplier idempotency (owner: infra/team-quota).
- Add monitoring alerts for per-tenant sudden delta in computed quota > 20%.
- Postmortem draft attached; will iterate and share final within 72 hours.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-v1.pdf (PDF)

—Dev
Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Runtime, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-02-14T15:20:00Z
Subject: Customer update: mitigation complete and proposed next steps

Laura — following up with a customer-facing summary:

What happened: an internal config rollout unintentionally caused tenant quota to be double-counted for a subset of traffic patterns.
What we did: immediate bypass + rollback completed; failures returned to baseline by ~14:50Z.
What we propose:
- Formal postmortem delivered by Feb 17 (we'll share earlier if ready).
- Goodwill credit for the affected window (we're proposing a 30% credit on usage during the outage; final details below).
- Optional technical deep-dive call with our infra leads (we can do Wed 2/18 or Thu 2/19).

Please confirm if the credit proposal and the Thursday deep-dive would work for Novelle. We'll also share the internal postmortem link once it's finalized.

Apologies again for the disruption — we understand this impacted your SLAs and are focused on preventing recurrence.

—Rishi
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@novellehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, procurement@novellehealth.com
Date: 2026-02-18T15:00:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary and remediation complete (Novelle Health)

Hi Laura — attaching the final post-incident summary and our remediation checklist. Summary highlights:
- Timeline: incident began 2026-02-14T13:50Z (first errors) — mitigation applied 2026-02-14T14:38Z — rollback complete 14:49Z.
- Root cause: misapplied tenant multiplier during a config rollout; double-counting at quota eval.
- Fixes deployed: rollback of rollout, idempotency checks, new unit/integration tests, monitoring alert for per-tenant quota deltas, and a staged rollout gating process.
- Customer impact: elevated 429s for ~38 minutes; estimated affected token usage window: 08:50–09:28 ET.
- Compensation: we applied a goodwill credit equal to 30% of usage for the affected hour; credit notice attached.

Links: postmortem (internal): https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/novelle-2026-02-14
Support ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/INC-2026-0458

Attachments: postmortem-final.pdf (PDF), redwood-credit-notice.pdf (PDF)

If you'd like a recording of the infra deep-dive or an FAQ for your SREs, we can prepare that. Thanks for working with us through this — we value the partnership.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
